sentences.text:
This Appeal filed by Insurer under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, takes exception to the judgment and award dated 11.11.2022 passed in M.A.C.P No. 1274/2018, whereby the learned Tribunal has allowed the claim petition filed by claimant for injury claim FA-190-2023 (B) +.odt and granted total compensation of Rs. 1,04,19,057/- with interest @ 7% p.a.
2.

The facts, which led to the filing of the Appeal, can be narrated in brief as under:
On 13.05.2018 claimant was proceeding on Activa Scooter from Antop Hill towards KEM Hospital.

When he reached the spot of accident, one motor dumper bearing no.
MH-43-Y-5105 came in high and excessive speed an dashed to the scooter of the claimant from behind.
As a result of the same, claimant fell down on the road and left wheel of the dumper ran over his foot.
In the said accident, he sustained serious injuries, which has resulted into amputation of his left leg.
He required hospitalization.
On the basis of the report, offence came to be registered vide Crime No. 140/2018 with Matunga Police Station against the driver of the dumper for negligent driving.
Claimant was aged 40 years old and was doing business of shoe making and was earning Rs. 60,000/- per month.
On different heads, compensation of Rs. 1,10,00,000/- was claimed.
3. Owner of the dumper failed to appear in spite of service of notice and hence, claim proceeded ex parte against him before Tribunal.
In this Appeal also owner has failed to cause appearance.
Insurer opposed the claim by filing written statement at Exhibit 14.
Insurer denied all averments made by the claimants and it is contended that the claim petition is bad for FA-190-2023 (B) +.odt non joinder of driver of the dumper as party to the proceedings.
It is claimed that accident has occurred due to the contributory negligence on the part of the claimant himself.
On these amongst other grounds, dismissal of the claim petition was sought.
4. Claimant examined himself at Exhibit 16 and placed reliance on police papers to support his claim.

In order to prove injuries, disability and medical expenses, he examined Dr. Tariq Palla,
Exhibit 31 and led evidence of Ahmed Pathan Exhibit 54, Shamsuddin Shaikh Exhibit 56 and also led evidence of Dr. Zahid M. Jaish Khan Exhibit 59.
To substantiate income, apart from testimony of claimant himself, he placed reliance on evidence of Ravi Kumar, Inspector of Income Tax Department Exhibit 44.
Through this witness, income tax returns for assessment years 2015-2016 till 2019-2020 were proved.
Insurer failed to led any evidence before Tribunal.
As Tribunal allowed the claim, present Appeal.
5. Learned Counsel for the Appellant Insurer submits that the Tribunal has failed to take into consideration the negligence on the part of the claimant himself with regard to occurrence of accident.
In this regard, she drew attention of the Court to the admission given by claimant in his cross-examination that driver of the dumper blew horn, however, he did not heard the same.
It is her contention that claimant is required to be held liable for contributory negligence for causing accident.
On the point of FA-190-2023 (B) +.odt quantum, it is argued that claimant has failed to prove income.

In this regard, reference is made to income tax returns placed on record, which according to her, indicate that the income from other source is major portion and hence, it cannot Icici Lombard General Insurance Co. ... vs Mr. Arif Akbar Pathan And Anr. on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53689524/
2 be considered as income of the deceased from his business.

sentences.text:
With regard to business,
cross-examination of claimant is referred in order to argue that the claimant had no shop of his own and to show rented shop, there is no documentary evidence such as lease agreement, rent agreement, etc placed on record.
It is contended that merely because on the basis of income tax returns, Tribunal ought not to have accepted the income of the claimant @ Rs. 60,000/- per month.
It is further argued that Tribunal has not considered the evidence led by the claimant with regard to attendant as well as the hospitalization and medical expenses in proper perspective.
It is submitted that merely on the basis of statements of witnesses that they worked as attendant, claim could not have been allowed.
It is further argued that the Tribunal once granted future prospects, was precluded from granting any compensation towards loss of income.
It is also argued that the Tribunal has committed error in granting compensation of Rs. 4,36,760/- towards modular leg prosthesis.
On these amongst other submissions, interference in the impugned order is sought.
6. Learned Counsel for Claimants supported the impugned judgment and award.
It is his submission that the cross-examination FA-190-2023 (B) +.odt conducted of claimant does not indicate any challenge to the income of the claimant.
It is argued that there is corroboration of evidence of oath of claimant by income tax returns and hence, Tribunal was justified in accepting the income of the claimant @ Rs. 60,000/- per month.

It is further argued that in view of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and Another, (2011) 1 SCC 343, the pecuniary damages include loss of earning during the period of treatment so also loss of future earning on the count of permanent disability.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and Another, (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In this regard, he drew attention of the Court to evidence of Dr. Palla,
which according to him, indicate that till 2022 claimant was taking treatment and hence, amount of compensation of Rs. 9,00,000/- towards the same does not require interference.
7. In so far as issue of negligence, there is no pleading in written statement about the claimant himself being negligent in occurrence of accident.

Even otherwise, mere acceptance on his part of having not heard horn blown by driver of the dumper, would not lead to the conclusion that the claimant himself was negligent in driving scooter nor from this admission it can be inferred that dumper was driven carefully.
Owner has failed to cause appearance before the Tribunal and Insurer has failed to led any evidence to hold that the claimant himself was negligent in causing of the accident.
It was, therefore, necessary for the Insurer to examine the FA-190-2023 (B) +.odt driver of the dumper in order to show that the said vehicle was driven by following traffic rules.
In absence of leading as well as evidence, it cannot be held that claimant was negligence in any manner and has contributed in the occurrence of the accident.

8. As far as the income of the claimant is concerned, he deposed on oath about he earning Rs.
60,000/- per month from the business of shoe making.
Though it is suggested to the claimant in the cross-examination that he has not undertaken any formal training in that regard, however, no dispute is made about he was doing the said business.
In fact, from the cross-examination it has come on record that the claimant is having rented shop from where business used to be conducted.
This oral testimony of the claimant gets corroborated from the income tax returns, which are duly proved by cross-examination of Inspector of Income Tax Department.
In the cross-examination, no question has been raised with regard to the genuineness of the income tax returns.
Similarly, what has been argued by the learned Counsel for the Appellant before this Court, is without any Icici Lombard General Insurance Co. ... vs Mr. Arif Akbar Pathan And Anr.

3 foundation being led before the Tribunal by way of cross-examination of claimant as well as Inspector of Income Tax Department.
This Court, therefore, has no hesitation to hold that the Tribunal was right in accepting income of claimant @ Rs. 60,000/- per month.

Needless to say that in view of judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Company FA-190-2023 (B)
+.odt Limited vs. Pranay Sethi, AIR 2017 SC 5157, claimant is entitled for future prospects, which has been rightly taken into consideration and owing to the age of the claimant, compensation amount derived is correct.
9. Coming to the issue of loss of actual income, there is substance in the contention of learned Counsel for the Claimant that in addition to future earnings on account of permanent disability, the claimant is entitled for loss of earning during the period of treatment.

entities.text:
National Insurance Company FA-190-2023 (B)
+.odt Limited vs. Pranay Sethi, AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In this regard, though evidence of Dr. Palla indicates that thrice claimant was required to be admitted in the hospital,
however, out of these three admissions, first two admissions are of year 2018 i.e. within two months of occurrence of accident.
For the third time, hospitalization was required for four days between 16.07.2020 to 20.07.2020.
Dr. Palla specifically does not state for the purpose for which he was admitted in the hospital for third time.

Having regard to the fact that the accident occurred on 13.05.2018 and that within a period of two months he was required to be hospitalized twice, the Tribunal would have been justified in granting compensation for loss of income for the said period.
Having regard to the judgment in case of Raj Kumar (supra), claimant would be entitled to receive Rs. 1,20,000/- only for loss of income during period of treatment instead of Rs. 9,00,000/-.
10. There is evidence on record to indicate that claimant suffered amputation of leg and was required to go for artificial limb.
Though it is FA-190-2023 (B) +.odt argued on behalf of Appellant that there is no evidence to indicate that subsequently any artificial limb obtained by claimant.
However, it is pertinent to note that once claimant has lost his leg and is required artificial limb, the said limb would have maximum life of 4 to 5 years.
Having regard to the age of the claimant and requirement of artificial limbs in future, compensation of Rs. 4,36,760/- granted by Tribunal is justified and requires no interference.

11. The aforesaid discussion indicates that the judgment and awarded passed by the Tribunal deserves modification to the extent of granting compensation towards loss of income @ Rs.
1,20,000/- instead of Rs. 9,00,000/-.

12. In view of above, following order is passed:
ORDER (a) Appeal is partly allowed.
Impugned judgment and award dated 11.11.2022 passed in M.A.C.P No. 1274/2018 is modified.
Total compensation is determined to the tune of Rs. 96,39,057/- along with interest at 7% per annum.
(b) Rest of judgment and award to remain unchanged.
(c) Modified award be prepared accordingly.
